strongest_angle: Examine how average weekly sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific reached record highs during October 2026 weeks ahead of the December peak, with the weekly relative Niño 3.4 index hitting +2.81°C as reported by Australia's Bureau of Meteorology and the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

key_facts.fact: The Copernicus Climate Change Service reported that sea surface temperatures in a region of the Pacific reached 29.70C in September 2026.
Australia's Bureau of Meteorology stated that the weekly relative Niño 3.4 index reached +2.81°C during the week ending on October 11, 2026.

The World Meteorological Organization based in Geneva, Switzerland, forecast that sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific will increase to record levels during October-November-December 2026.
